core_principles.text: Stand upright with feet a comfortable width apart and the back against a wall to stabilize the body during the curl.
Use an elbow stabilizing plate or maintain strict elbow positioning to ensure that the full range of motion of the elbow joint is achieved and to prevent swinging the elbows.
Control the movement by performing both the concentric and eccentric phases of the curl with a controlled tempo, such as approximately one second for each phase.

common_mistakes.text: Swinging the elbows during the bicep curl instead of keeping them stabilized.
Failing to achieve the full range of motion of the elbow joint during each repetition.

specific_findings.text: A 21-year-old female performing 3 sets of bilateral dumbbell bicep curls to failure at 30% 1RM (totaling 143 repetitions) developed exertional rhabdomyolysis with a peak creatine kinase (CK) concentration of approximately 12,200 U/L.
Acute swelling immediately after high-repetition bicep curls to failure increased biceps muscle thickness by 17.6% (from 1.943 cm to 2.285 cm).

Echo intensity of the biceps brachii, a surrogate measure of muscle damage and edema, increased by 10.8% immediately post-exercise, peaked at 34.9% above baseline at 4 days post-exercise, and remained 16.7% elevated at 6 days post-exercise.

consequences.text: Performing high-repetition bicep curls to failure can result in severe muscle damage and swelling proximal to the elbows, rendering the lifter temporarily unable to fully extend their forearms.

source: data\bicep-curl\Exertional Rhabdomyolysis in a 21-year-old, Healthy Female after Performing Three Sets of the Biceps Curl Exercise to Failure with 30% 1rm A Case Report.pdf [part 3/4]

core_principles.text: Exercising muscles at a longer length by completing a full range of motion of the elbow joint produces more muscle damage.

common_mistakes.text: Performing low-load, high-repetition resistance exercise to failure significantly increases the time the muscle is under tension and the total work performed, which can cause severe muscle damage.

specific_findings.text: A 21-year-old healthy female was diagnosed with exertional rhabdomyolysis after completing 3 sets of bilateral dumbbell biceps curls at 30% 1RM (3.4 kg) for 143 total repetitions, resulting in a peak creatine kinase (CK) concentration of approximately 12,200 U/L.

consequences.text: Performing exercises that place the muscle at a longer length through a full range of motion can increase muscle damage and potentially lead to exertional rhabdomyolysis.

source: data\bicep-curl\Exertional Rhabdomyolysis in a 21-year-old, Healthy Female after Performing Three Sets of the Biceps Curl Exercise to Failure with 30% 1rm A Case Report.pdf [part 4/4]
